## v0.1 — First release

`#########·` 88% · 15 of 17 done · due 2026-11-20

## v0.2 — Saves in seconds

`#·········` 10% · 1 of 10 done · due 2026-12-18

Changing one file in a multi-gigabyte ZIP saves in seconds, because everything unchanged is copied byte for byte instead of being compressed again.

### backlog

- [ ] `0017` Copy unchanged ZIP entries verbatim: our own writer, or libarchive? <sup>spike · p0 · archive</sup>
- [ ] `0018` ZipCatalog: read a ZIP's central directory without unpacking <sup>feature · p0 · archive</sup>
- [ ] `0019` ZipWriter: write a ZIP that copies unchanged entries byte for byte <sup>feature · p0 · archive</sup>
- [ ] `0020` Know which workspace files still match their archive entry <sup>feature · p0 · document</sup>
- [ ] `0021` Save through ZipWriter so small changes to big archives save in seconds <sup>feature · p0 · document</sup>
- [ ] `0022` Benchmarks with budgets for opening, listing, and saving <sup>feature · p1 · quality</sup>
- [ ] `0023` Readable errors for every failure a user can hit <sup>feature · p1 · document</sup>
- [ ] `0024` Show the version and build from the release tag in About <sup>feature · p2 · shell</sup>
- [ ] `0057` Read Deflate64 ZIPs, which Windows makes for large files <sup>feature · p2 · archive</sup>

### done

- [x] `0059` Give Zipboy a look of its own <sup>feature · p1 · shell</sup>

## v0.3 — Opens instantly

`··········` 0% · 0 of 5 done · due 2027-01-29

Any ZIP, however large, shows its contents in under a second and costs no disk space until a file inside is actually previewed, opened, or dragged out.

### backlog

- [ ] `0025` What breaks if files exist only once they're used? <sup>spike · p0 · document</sup>
- [ ] `0026` Browse a ZIP from its catalog before anything is unpacked <sup>feature · p0 · browser</sup>
- [ ] `0027` Unpack an entry the first time it's previewed, opened, or copied <sup>feature · p0 · document</sup>
- [ ] `0028` Drag out with file promises so entries arrive whole <sup>feature · p1 · browser</sup>
- [ ] `0029` Show and cancel progress for long adds and extracts <sup>feature · p1 · shell</sup>

## v0.4 — Part of the Mac

`··········` 0% · 0 of 10 done · due 2027-03-12

Zipboy works from the Finder as well as in its own window: Quick Look shows what's in an archive, Quick Actions compress and extract, updates arrive by themselves, and every flow works with VoiceOver and the keyboard alone.

### backlog

- [ ] `0030` Can SwiftPM and Command Line Tools build and sign a Quick Look extension? <sup>spike · p0 · system</sup>
- [ ] `0031` Space in Finder shows what's inside an archive <sup>feature · p0 · system</sup>
- [ ] `0032` Finder Quick Actions: Compress with Zipboy and Extract Here <sup>feature · p0 · system</sup>
- [ ] `0033` Auto-updates: Sparkle, or a release-feed check of our own? <sup>spike · p1 · distribution</sup>
- [ ] `0034` Updates arrive without the user doing anything <sup>feature · p1 · distribution</sup>
- [ ] `0035` VoiceOver and full keyboard access across every flow <sup>feature · p0 · quality</sup>

- [ ] `0037` Spring-loaded folders and a drop target on the empty window <sup>feature · p2 · browser</sup>
- [ ] `0038` Offer once to open ZIPs with Zipboy <sup>feature · p2 · system</sup>
- [ ] `0039` Remember an archive's password in the Keychain, if asked <sup>feature · p3 · document</sup>

## v1.0 — The promise

`··········` 0% · 0 of 6 done · due 2027-04-23

An archive behaves like a Finder folder, reliably, for anyone: hardened against hostile archives, documented, and proven by a public beta. No new features.

### backlog

- [ ] `0040` Fuzz ZipCatalog and the libarchive reading path <sup>chore · p0 · quality</sup>
- [ ] `0041` Hostile archives: zip bombs, traversal, link chains, and absurd sizes <sup>feature · p0 · archive</sup>

- [ ] `0043` A landing page with the download, screenshots, and the format table <sup>docs · p1 · distribution</sup>
- [ ] `0044` A two-week public beta with every crash and data-loss report closed <sup>chore · p0 · quality</sup>
- [ ] `0045` Release checklist and the v1.0 tag <sup>chore · p0 · distribution</sup>
